items.summary: Tencent released DFly2, a speculative-decoding tool that predicts several tokens ahead for the main model to verify. Tencent reports up to 81% higher throughput for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at a 64k-token context and up to 4.2x faster results on some agent tasks — a useful trick when compute is tight.
items.title: Tencent open-sources DFly2, reporting up to 81% higher DeepSeek throughput

items.summary: OpenAI added nine mathematics manuscripts to GitHub on 24 November, the same day Anthropic published a 70-page Claude-authored proof attempt for VP ≠ VNP. Both claims are striking, but neither has completed peer review yet, so treat them as preprints to scrutinise, not settled results.
items.title: OpenAI posts nine maths papers as Anthropic shares a VP vs VNP proof — peer review pending

items.summary: DeepL announced Aure v2 at its first Tokyo event on 26 November and made it available immediately. Instead of transcribing then translating then synthesising, it maps spoken input directly to speech in another language — watch latency and dialect handling in real tests.
items.title: DeepL launches Aure v2 for direct speech-to-speech translation

items.summary: Kioxia's 26 November proof of concept pairs NVIDIA SCADA software with SSDs to stretch effective GPU memory beyond on-card VRAM. If the latency holds up, consumer and workstation cards could run models that currently do not fit — relevant for local ML work on modest hardware.
items.title: Kioxia and NVIDIA test SSD-backed GPU memory expansion

items.summary: Canada added C$700 million to its AI Compute Access Fund, taking the total to C$1 billion, with support covering up to 80% of eligible compute costs for businesses using qualifying sovereign cloud providers. Another sign that subsidised compute is becoming industrial policy, not just cloud pricing.
items.title: Canada tops up AI Compute Access Fund to C$1 billion

items.summary: GTA 6 generated about £32 million in UK physical sales in three days, the biggest physical release there since 2019 — even though boxed editions contain download codes rather than discs. Physical retail is not dead; it has become a code-delivery channel for mega-launches.
items.title: GTA 6 posts the UK's biggest physical game launch since 2019

items.summary: Until the 2 December reset, GTA Online adds four Kortz Center Heist primary targets with a GTA$400,000 no-death bonus, 4x payouts on Freemode Events, 3x on stunt/community races, and the Vapid Caracara 6x6 on the casino podium. The LS Car Meet prize ride needs race wins on four consecutive days, so start early.
items.title: GTA Online weekly update (26 Nov–2 Dec): new Kortz Center targets, up to 4x payouts

items.summary: In a vote held during GTA 6's launch week, about 75% of Rockstar workers voted against formal union recognition, so the studio will not recognise union members as a bargaining unit. Organisers say the result is not a retreat — expect this labour story to continue alongside the sales records.
items.title: Rockstar staff vote 75% against union recognition

items.summary: Rockstar brought in a former Gran Turismo professional to help master GTA 6's car handling, according to Push Square reporting on 27 November. A nice Shayegan-style fact: the most arcade-famous driving series borrowed a sim racer's feel for Leonida's roads.
items.title: GTA fact: car handling was tuned with help from a Gran Turismo pro

items.summary: Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson argues the new Criminal Profile system does not limit player freedom, responding to mixed reactions since launch. The design question for players: do consequences for crime deepen role-play, or just add friction? Leonida will decide.
items.title: Rockstar defends GTA 6's Criminal Profile system as more freeing, not less
